rule: Every link goes to the maker's own site. PointCast never hosts someone else's installer or re-uploads someone else's picture. Rights are the source's to state — the note here is a pointer, not a license.

shelves.title: Free photographs
shelves.dek: Working photo libraries. Search runs on their site, with whatever you typed above.

entries.name: Unsplash
entries.note: Free to use, commercial included, no credit required. You can't resell unaltered copies or build a rival library.

entries.name: Pexels
entries.note: Photos and video. Same shape as Unsplash: free, no credit required, no reselling as-is.

entries.name: Pixabay
entries.note: Photos, illustrations, vectors, some music. Skip the sponsored row at the top.

entries.name: Openverse
entries.note: WordPress's search engine over 800M openly licensed images and audio. Filter by license before you use.

entries.name: Wikimedia Commons
entries.note: The largest free media library there is. Every file states its own license — read it.

entries.name: rawpixel public domain
entries.note: Cleaned-up scans of public-domain illustration — botanicals, ukiyo-e, vintage posters. Free account for full size.

shelves.title: Museum open access
shelves.dek: Institutions that released their public-domain holdings at full resolution. The first four are wired into the finder above.

entries.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
entries.note: 490,000+ works marked Open Access. Look for the OA icon under the image.

entries.name: Art Institute of Chicago
entries.note: Hopper-era America, Japanese prints, the Impressionists. Clean IIIF image server.

entries.name: Cleveland Museum of Art
entries.note: Print-size JPEGs and full TIFFs for 30,000+ works. The most generous file sizes of the lot.

entries.name: NASA Image and Video Library
entries.note: NASA imagery is usually free to use; logos and identifiable people are the exceptions. Check the media guidelines.

entries.name: The Getty — Open Content
entries.note: Up the 405 from here. 88,000+ images, no permission required.

entries.name: LACMA collections
entries.note: The county museum. Filter to public-domain images for free high-resolution downloads.

entries.name: National Gallery of Art
entries.note: Washington's gallery — 50,000+ open images, plus the full collection dataset on GitHub.

entries.name: Smithsonian Open Access
entries.note: Millions of 2D and 3D items across 21 museums, nine research centers, and the zoo.

entries.name: Rijksmuseum
entries.note: Rembrandt and Vermeer at absurd resolution. Download straight from the object page.

entries.name: Paris Musées
entries.note: Fourteen city museums of Paris. Each download arrives with its own credit sheet.

entries.name: Library of Congress — Free to Use
entries.note: Curated sets: travel posters, dogs, lighthouses, baseball cards. Already sorted for you.

entries.name: NYPL Digital Collections
entries.note: Tick “Search only public domain materials.” Maps, menus, stereographs, fashion plates.

entries.name: Biodiversity Heritage Library
entries.note: Four centuries of natural-history illustration. If you want a hummingbird plate, start here.

entries.name: Europeana
entries.note: One search across thousands of European archives. The reusability filter is the whole trick.

entries.name: The Public Domain Review
entries.note: Not a library — a journal that finds the strange and beautiful things and tells you where they live.

shelves.title: Type, icons, marks
shelves.dek: Open-licensed letters and pictograms you can ship in a product.

entries.name: Google Fonts
entries.note: 1,800+ open families. Download the files and self-host rather than hot-linking.

entries.name: The League of Moveable Type
entries.note: The first open-source type foundry. Small shelf, all keepers — League Gothic, Raleway, Ostrich Sans.

entries.name: Velvetyne
entries.note: French libre foundry. The weird ones. Good for a poster, risky for a paragraph.

entries.name: Departure Mono
entries.note: Pixel monospace with real manners. It's the mono in Sparrow.

entries.name: Lucide
entries.note: 1,500+ consistent stroke icons. The maintained fork of Feather.

entries.name: Phosphor Icons
entries.note: Six weights of every icon, including duotone.

entries.name: Heroicons
entries.note: From the Tailwind people. Small set, copy-paste SVG.

entries.name: OpenMoji
entries.note: Open-source emoji drawn as one family. Credit and share-alike apply.

entries.name: Nouns
entries.note: One Noun a day, forever, all public domain. Any head by number at noun.pics — the town uses them everywhere.

shelves.title: Sound, books, film
shelves.dek: Things to listen to, read, and cut up.

entries.name: Freesound
entries.note: Field recordings and one-shots. Filter to CC0 if you don't want to keep a credits file.

entries.name: Musopen
entries.note: Classical recordings and sheet music with the rights cleared.

entries.name: Free Music Archive
entries.note: Curated since WFMU started it in 2009. Check each track's license.

entries.name: Project Gutenberg
entries.note: 75,000+ books. Plain, fast, unkillable.

entries.name: Standard Ebooks
entries.note: Gutenberg's texts, properly typeset and proofed. The edition you actually want on a reader.

entries.name: LibriVox
entries.note: Volunteer-read audiobooks of public-domain books. Quality varies; the good readers are very good.

entries.name: Internet Archive
entries.note: Everything. Rights are item by item — check the panel on the right.

entries.name: Prelinger Archives
entries.note: Thousands of industrial, educational, and home films. Free to download and reuse.

shelves.title: 3D, maps, data
shelves.dek: Raw material for building a world.

entries.name: Poly Haven
entries.note: HDRIs, textures, and models. No account, no paywall, no catch.

entries.name: Kenney
entries.note: 40,000+ game assets — isometric tiles, UI packs, sound. The fastest way to a playable prototype.

entries.name: OpenGameArt
entries.note: Community sprites, tiles, and music. License is on every page; CC0 filter available.

entries.name: Smithsonian 3D
entries.note: Scanned objects you can spin, download, and print — from a mammoth to the Apollo 11 module.

entries.name: OpenStreetMap
entries.note: The map of the world that anyone can edit. Credit “© OpenStreetMap contributors.”

entries.name: Natural Earth
entries.note: Clean world map data at three scales. Coastlines, borders, rivers, shaded relief.

entries.name: NOAA NCEI
entries.note: Weather and climate records going back as far as anyone wrote them down. Station data, buoys, radar archives.

entries.name: Data.gov
entries.note: The federal catalog. 300,000+ datasets of wildly uneven usefulness.

shelves.title: Free software
shelves.dek: Open-source programs with long track records. Links go to the project's own download page — never a mirror, never a “free download” site.

entries.name: Firefox
entries.note: The browser that isn't owned by an ad company.

entries.name: Thunderbird
entries.note: Desktop mail, calendars, and feeds. Still here, recently much better.

entries.name: Signal
entries.note: Private messaging, run by a nonprofit.

entries.name: Bitwarden
entries.note: Password manager. Open source, audited, free tier is the whole product.

entries.name: KeePassXC
entries.note: Password manager that never touches a server. Your vault is a file you keep.

entries.name: VLC
entries.note: Plays everything. Get it from VideoLAN only — fake VLC installers are everywhere.

entries.name: HandBrake
entries.note: Convert video to something every device can play.

entries.name: OBS Studio
entries.note: Recording and live streaming. What the broadcast would run on.

entries.name: Audacity
entries.note: Record, cut, and clean audio.

entries.name: Blender
entries.note: 3D, animation, video editing. Studio-grade and free.

entries.name: Krita
entries.note: Digital painting, made by painters.

entries.name: GIMP
entries.note: Photo editing. Version 3 finally fixed the things you remember hating.

entries.name: Inkscape
entries.note: Vector drawing. Opens and saves real SVG.

entries.name: Piskel
entries.note: Pixel-art sprite editor that runs in a tab. Nothing to install.

entries.name: Godot
entries.note: A full game engine with no royalties and no strings.

entries.name: LibreOffice
entries.note: Documents, spreadsheets, slides. Opens the Office files people send you.

entries.name: Syncthing
entries.note: Keep folders in sync between your own machines, with no cloud in the middle.

entries.name: Homebrew
entries.note: The Mac package manager. One line in Terminal, then everything else is one line too.
